questions.question: An agent runs each command with a fresh subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True). What goes wrong with 'cd app' then 'ls'?
options: The cd happens in a shell that exits; the next command runs in the original directory
questions.explanation: A persistent shell keeps cwd and environment between commands.

questions.question: Why is every command wrapped as '{ cmd\n} < /dev/null'?
options: So a command that reads stdin gets end-of-file instead of swallowing the agent's next commands
questions.explanation: The shell's stdin is the agent's command pipe. Commands must not read from it.

questions.question: How does the shell wrapper know a command finished and what its exit code was?
options: It prints a random end marker followed by $? and reads until the marker appears
questions.explanation: The unique marker separates commands' output and carries the exit code.

questions.question: 'ls && rm -rf ~' is one string. What does the policy do?
options: Allows it because it starts with ls
Denies it: the whole command matches the recursive-delete-of-home pattern, and each segment is checked
questions.explanation: Compound commands are checked as a whole and segment by segment.

questions.question: 'sleep 30' times out. What must the agent be told?
options: That the shell was restarted, so the working directory and exported variables were reset
questions.explanation: A silent restart leaves the model with a wrong picture of its environment.

questions.question: Why isn't a pattern-matching command policy enough on its own?
options: Shells can hide commands (encoding, eval, scripts), so policies catch the obvious; a container must be the real boundary
questions.explanation: Use the policy to reduce risk and noise, and isolation to bound the damage.
